lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice giving reasons in a past story with eftersom or för att.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: A colleague explains why a simple plan changed.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Explaining reasons and consequences in everyday conversation.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik discuss a plan from yesterday that changed because of weather, time, or transport.

main_focus.name: reason clauses with eftersom and för att
main_focus.description: Use a subordinate reason clause to explain why something happened or changed.
model_examples: Vi stannade hemma eftersom det regnade.
Jag tog bussen för att tåget var sent.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use eftersom or för att naturally 3 times in the dialogue.

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use reason words with practical causes like weather, timing, or transport.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person asks why a plan did not happen as expected.
dialogue_shape.middle: The reason is explained with one or two concrete causes and a result.
dialogue_shape.ending: They agree that the changed plan was understandable or better.

target_complexity.repetition: reason clauses should recur without becoming a grammar drill

focus: the final result of the changed plan

sentence_focus: one sentence explaining a changed plan
one sentence with därför as a result
one sentence about weather or transport causing a change
